content.title: About
content.content: Bacon is smoked or cured pork belly that is widely used in cooking to add a rich, savory flavor and aroma to dishes. When paired with vegetables, bacon contributes smoky notes, a juicy texture, and enhances the overall taste profile.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bacon dates back to ancient Rome, where pork was salted and dried for preservation.
The word “bacon” comes from the Old French “bacon,” meaning “pork.”
In the United States, more than 18 million tons of bacon are consumed each year.
Bacon is a staple in one‑pot meals such as soups, stews, casseroles, and salads.
Cold‑smoked and hot‑smoked methods produce different flavors and textures in bacon.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Bacon provides complete animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 supports the nervous system and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc is important for immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Provides iron
items.content: Iron in bacon helps maintain healthy hemoglobin levels.

items.title: Contains selenium
items.content: Selenium has antioxidant properties and supports thyroid health.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Bacon is often heavily salted, which can raise blood pressure if consumed in excess.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Large amounts of saturated fat may contribute to cardiovascular disease.

items.title: Nitrates and nitrites
items.content: Curing and smoking can introduce nitrates/nitrites, which in high doses are considered potentially carcinogenic.

items.title: Pork allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to pork.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Crisp the bacon in a pan and add it to vegetable salads, stews, casseroles, or use it as a flavor base for sauces. For a lighter option, slice thinly, quick‑sauté, and toss with sautéed vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep bacon refrigerated at 0 °C–4 °C in its original packaging or an airtight container for 5–7 days. For longer storage, freeze in a zip‑lock bag at –18 °C, where it remains good for up to 6 months. Before use, check for off‑odors or discoloration—signs of spoilage include sour smell and grayish color.
